close_reason: Applied the only viable change: replaced 'b_rdns.iter()' with 'b_rdns' inside the zip() at line 1369. The other two sites flagged in the issue (current.iter() at ~2582, rdn.0.iter() at ~2973) cannot be migrated: 'current' is a &mut Vec from a &mut binding so &current resolves to &&mut Vec, and rdn.0 is a SetOfVec<AttributeTypeAndValue> which does NOT implement IntoIterator for &T. Verified by compile failure (E0277) on those rewrites. The issue's claim that all three were trivial migrations was incorrect; the two non-migratable sites are correct as-is.
description:
Pass 2 idiom finding under epic PKIX-qwzx.

Three sites in `pkix-path/src/lib.rs` use `for x in y.iter() { ... }` where
`for x in &y { ... }` is idiomatic. Rust 2018+ implicitly converts `&Vec<T>`
into an iterator of `&T` via `IntoIterator`; the explicit `.iter()` is
redundant.

Sites:

`pkix-path/src/lib.rs:1365`:
```rust
for (a_rdn, b_rdn) in a_rdns.iter().zip(b_rdns.iter()) {
```
Could be: `for (a_rdn, b_rdn) in a_rdns.iter().zip(b_rdns) {` (at minimum drop
the second `.iter()`).

`pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2578`:
```rust
for c in current.iter() {
```
Should be: `for c in &current {` — assuming `current` is the local
`Vec<...>` from line ~2570 (the `let current = ...;` binding).

`pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2969`:
```rust
for ava in rdn.0.iter() {
```
Should be: `for ava in &rdn.0 {` — `rdn.0` is a `SetOfVec<...>` whose
`&` reference iterates `&AttributeTypeAndValue`.

These are caught by `clippy::explicit_iter_loop` (style category, default-warn);
they only escape current CI because `pkix-path/src/lib.rs:4` uses
`#![warn(missing_docs, rust_2018_idioms)]` rather than `#![warn(clippy::style)]`.
The lint is independent of any pedantic/nursery tier.

Fix: rewrite each site to use the implicit `IntoIterator for &T` form. No
behavior change.
title: (IDIOM) P4: for x in y.iter() instead of for x in &y at three sites in pkix-path
